content.value_statement: PyTorch contributors need docstrings that match project conventions and render correctly in Sphinx. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to write concise reStructuredText docstrings with signatures, arguments, examples, math, and cross-references.
actual_capabilities: Formats PyTorch docstrings as raw reStructuredText strings with a signature first line.
Documents Args, Keyword args, Returns, notes, warnings, and examples using PyTorch conventions.
Adds Sphinx cross-references for classes, functions, methods, attributes, math, and refs.
Shows patterns for Python functions, C-bound _add_docstr entries, in-place variants, and aliases.
Includes guidance for tensor shapes, LaTeX math, reusable argument text, and template insertion.
Provides a checklist for reviewing PyTorch docstrings before submission.
limitations: Focuses on PyTorch documentation conventions, not NumPy or Google docstring styles.
Does not run tests, build docs, or verify that examples execute.
Requires accurate function behavior, argument types, and edge cases from the user.
Does not fetch remote documentation or inspect files unless the host agent is asked.

use_cases.title: Document new tensor APIs
use_cases.description: Create PyTorch-style docstrings for new functions before submitting a pull request.

use_cases.title: Align library documentation
use_cases.description: Make custom PyTorch extension documentation follow familiar torch formatting and examples.

use_cases.title: Review documentation changes
use_cases.description: Check docstrings for signatures, argument sections, cross-references, examples, and formatting gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Docstring
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one simple function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PyTorch-style docstring for this function. Include the signature line, a short description, Args, Returns, and one example.

prompt_templates.title: Add Sphinx References
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this docstring to use PyTorch Sphinx roles for related classes, functions, tensor methods, attributes, and inline math.

prompt_templates.title: Document Math Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PyTorch docstring for this tensor operation. Include LaTeX math, shape notes, Args, Returns, warnings, and runnable examples.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare C-Bound API Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Write documentation text for a C-bound PyTorch API using the project style. Include add_docstr guidance, reusable arguments, examples, and cross-references.

output_examples.input: Document a tensor normalization function with input, dimension, epsilon, and keepdim arguments.
output: A first-line signature with defaults and return type.
A concise behavior summary for normalization.
Args entries with tensor types, optional defaults, and shape notes.
A Returns entry describing the normalized tensor.
An Examples section using PyTorch interactive style.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed docstring for a PyTorch activation function.
output: A checklist of missing PyTorch formatting requirements.
Specific fixes for Sphinx roles, inline code, and math notation.
Suggestions for warnings, notes, and related module links.

output_examples.input: Create docs for an in-place tensor method and its alias.
output: A short in-place method description that references the original method.
Alias wording that points to the canonical function.

best_practices: Start with a complete signature line and keep it free of a final period.
Use raw strings and Sphinx roles so math, links, and inline code render correctly.
Include examples that show realistic tensor inputs and important edge cases.
anti_patterns: Mixing NumPy or Google docstring style with PyTorch reStructuredText conventions.
Omitting defaults, tensor shapes, or optional markers in argument descriptions.
Adding examples that cannot run or that hide important warning behavior.

faq.question: Is this skill only for PyTorch?
faq.answer: Yes. It targets PyTorch documentation conventions and may not fit other Python projects.

faq.question: Does it write NumPy-style docstrings?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Sphinx and reStructuredText patterns used by PyTorch.

faq.question: Can it document C-bound functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for PyTorch add_docstr patterns and related API entries.

faq.question: Does it verify examples by running them?
faq.answer: No. Users should run documentation tests or examples separately.

faq.question: Does it access project files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is guidance text. File access depends on the host agent and user request.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
